description: #3826 — READ-command differential over the block point-read surface: `get_block`, `get_blocks`, `first_child_for_blocks`, `batch_resolve` and `load_page_subtree`. The #763 snapshot already diffs these ROWS; what it does not diff is each command's own decision about them, so every step targets one such decision — whether a tombstone is served or filtered, whether a missing id is dropped or surfaced, whether `page_id` is the ROOT page or the immediate parent, and whether a subtree read walks `page_id` (grandchildren included) or just direct children. Every queried block is a SEED block, so ids are byte-identical on both stacks and the tokens are comparable.
name: query_point_reads_blocks

queries.comment: #3928 — the shipped `get_block` delegates to `get_active_block_inner`, whose SQL carries `AND deleted_at IS NULL`, so reading the block the ops just tombstoned is a `not_found` and NOT a served row. This step used to be named `get_block_serves_tombstone` and recorded the row: the harness arm was calling `get_block_inner`, the PERMISSIVE reader reserved for internal callers, and the mock had been aligned to the harness rather than to production — so the differential agreed with itself about a function the IPC surface never calls. Paired with `get_block_serves_a_live_block`, which is what stops an implementation that 404s EVERYTHING from passing this one. #3946 — `expect_error` is what says the refusal was the POINT: without it the same recording is indistinguishable from a step whose args were simply wrong, and the harness now refuses to author one.
queries.name: get_block_404s_on_tombstone

queries.comment: The other half of the pair: an ACTIVE block still comes back, so the `deleted_at IS NULL` predicate is pinned as a filter rather than as a blanket refusal. S4 is a grandchild (parent B3, page B1), so unlike the tombstone step its `page_id` attribute DOES pin the #1775 class — `page_id != parent_id` here, and a command that returned the immediate parent as the page would redden.
queries.name: get_block_serves_a_live_block

queries.comment: Three ids: a live grandchild, a tombstone, and an id that exists nowhere. `get_blocks_inner` documents both halves — no `deleted_at` filter, and unknown ids silently omitted — so a mock that filtered tombstones OR echoed a placeholder row for the unknown id reddens. Unordered: the backend's `id IN (json_each(…))` does not guarantee input order.
queries.name: get_blocks_keeps_tombstone_drops_missing

queries.comment: S1's position-1 child is the tombstone, so the first ACTIVE child is S3 — the CTE pre-filters `deleted_at IS NULL` before `ROW_NUMBER()`, and a mock ranking before filtering would answer B2 here. S2 is requested too and must be ABSENT from the map (a parent with no active children is omitted, not mapped to null).
queries.name: first_child_skips_tombstoned_first_sibling

queries.comment: The chip resolver keeps a tombstoned target and marks it `deleted: true` (the FE renders a broken chip from that flag) rather than dropping it; the unknown id IS dropped. `title` is the renamed `content` column — an id-only token could not see either projection.
queries.name: batch_resolve_flags_tombstone

queries.comment: `load_page_subtree_inner` selects on `page_id = root`, so the GRANDCHILD S4 is in the result even though its parent is S3 — a mock that listed direct children would drop it. The root itself and the tombstone are excluded. `ordered` because the sort key is `(position, id)` over seed blocks whose ids are byte-identical on both stacks. #3977 — S5 (page Beta) and its child S6 are the NEGATIVE CONTROL and the reason this step can fail at all: both are ACTIVE, both are in the same space, and both have `page_id != S1`, so the `page_id` predicate is the only thing that excludes them. Before they were seeded every active non-root block already had `page_id == S1`, and deleting the walk predicate from the mock changed nothing (measured: green across the whole frontend suite). S6 also sits at position 1, so a dropped predicate reorders the head of this `ordered` list, not just its tail.
queries.name: load_page_subtree_walks_page_id
